result.title: Interpreting Supervised Pairwise Graph Representations: Local Evidence, Confounding, and Provable Post-hoc Correction
result.summary: Supervised pairwise graph representations convert pairwise predictive relations into sample-specific graphs, but graph-level accuracy does not by itself show that higher-order topology carries the signal. In a controlled Transformer error-detection task, supervised pairwise graphs outperform attention-as-adjacency (ROC-AUC $0.839$ versus $0.559$; the comparable no-confidence pair is $0.687$ versus $0.559$), but their apparent advantage over model confidence disappears after controlling for sequence length, which is almost perfectly recoverable from the pooled hidden state ($R^2=0.9995$). On published HCP Emotion ensemble graphs, signed node aggregation already acts as an ensemble of supervised pairwise predictions. Edge magnitude alone is near chance; topology-aware augmentations change ROC-AUC by at most $0.004$, with only sign-separated degree showing small positive changes across all tested graph sizes, while a validation-tuned three-layer GCN provides no measurable improvement over the signed node-summary baseline. A Fisher post-hoc corrector satisfies its distribution-agnostic guarantees across the evaluated feature representations and remains stable under reduced labelled budgets; in a near-error-free fMRI calibration regime the bound correctly becomes statistically uninformative. A separate cross-attention analysis identifies a redundant reversal circuit and downstream EOS-timing and copy failures. Higher-order topology should therefore be credited only after local supervised evidence and recoverable nuisance variables have been excluded.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在受控 Transformer 错误检测任务与公开 HCP Emotion 图数据上，检验监督式成对图表示的高阶拓扑是否真正携带信号，发现其相对模型置信度的优势在控制序列长度后消失、边幅度接近随机水平，并给出 Fisher 事后校正及交叉注意力失败回路分析。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「从 pooled hidden state 几乎完美还原序列长度、再据此消去表观增益」的混杂控制与事后校正思路，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 表示的内容贡献与长度、位置等可解码冗余之间的贡献分配提供方法线索，需进一步确认能否迁移到多模态推理场景。
